caption: How the hi server is laid out. Admins set it up on a small always-on machine in the team's NetBird network. It listens only on its NetBird address and answers only requests signed by connected devices. It alone holds the team's keys: provider keys, Hugging Face tokens, the model key, and template tokens, with the devices, groups, and audit log. Its policy says per group what may be started, downloaded, or used, approves small requests on its own up to a price and time, and warns when a budget is crossed. It asks for approvals and reports through the team's Slack app, and serves connected devices managed machines, the team's model, its data, and private templates.
via: hi server init · provider add · run

key.text: A small always-on Linux machine in the team's NetBird network.
The service the team's devices talk to, and nothing else can.
Readable only by the account the server runs as; no user ever holds these keys.
Limits per group, so a student and an admin can share one server.
Where people approve, see their requests, and get reports.
People's machines and their agents, each known by its key; removing one ends its access.
